The NCW's fact-finding committee observed that victims were intimidated into silence due to a lack of formal complaint mechanisms and a toxic workplace environment.  The committee has recommended action for TCS’ failure to comply with the POSH Act, as well as measures to protect complainants and ensure a safe working environment.

recent_articles.title: The road to deliver women’s safety - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The case of **Sai Bhagirath**, son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs **Bandi Sanjay**, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act is being closely watched as a test of how **Telangana** handles crimes against women and children. The state government has taken several steps to address online and offline harassment, including launching the "Stand with Her" initiative and investigating cases of cyberbullying. However, the case highlights the challenge of balancing free expression with curbing online targeting and harassment, particularly for women in positions of power.  The incident has sparked protests demanding action from both women's groups and political parties.

recent_articles.title: Telangana BJP distances itself from POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son, calls it legal issue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** (BJP) in Telangana distanced itself from a POCSO case involving the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The state BJP president, N. Ramchander Rao, stated that the party has no connection to the matter and will investigate if any family member is involved.  Rao also addressed allegations of discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted during the recent Assembly elections, claiming it was a clean-up exercise approved by the Election Commission and Supreme Court. He asserted that the SIR aimed to eliminate "bogus" voters and that the results reflected the mandate of genuine voters.

recent_articles.title: Bandi Bhagirath’s case takes serious turn with Telangana CM ordering special team for comprehensive probe - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **A. Revanth Reddy**, **Telangana Chief Minister**, has demanded an immediate investigation into allegations of sexual harassment against the son of **Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar**, **Bandi Bhagirath**.  The Chief Minister, who is also the Home Minister, instructed the Director General of Police (DGP), **C.V. Anand**, to launch a probe into the case registered at Pet Basheerabad Police Station. The investigation follows allegations that the police have been slow to act on the complaint lodged by the alleged victim on May 8th.

recent_articles.title: Bandi urges BJP workers to not believe allegations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bandi Sanjay Kumar**, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, addressed allegations against him and his family, stating he would never engage in actions that harm the **BJP**.  He urged his supporters to disregard the accusations made by the **Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS)**.

recent_articles.title: Sub-inspector suspended - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mujeeb H.**, a sub-inspector at the Elamakkara police station, was suspended on Sunday after being booked in two separate cases for sexual harassment, intimidation, and attempted extortion. The alleged incidents occurred in 2025, involving misuse of a narcotics investigation to obtain a woman's phone number and make sexual advances. **H.** is currently absconding.

recent_articles.title: BRS leader Praveen Kumar demands SIT probe with women police officers into POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R.S. Praveen Kumar**, general secretary of the **Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS)**, has called for a Special Investigation Team (SIT) with senior women police officers to investigate the high-profile POCSO case against the son of Union Minister of State for Home **Bandi Sanjay**.  Kumar stated that the police delayed accepting the complaint from the victim's family for five hours and did not provide an acknowledgement until they threatened suicide at a meeting with the Prime Minister.

recent_articles.title: Research sheds light on GI’s murder of seven-year-old girl in Northern Ireland in 1944 | Northern Ireland | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: On September 25, 1944, **William Harrison**, a US soldier stationed in Northern Ireland, raped and murdered seven-year-old **Patsy Wylie**.  **Annie Kalotschke**, Patsy's niece, has spent decades researching the case and uncovering new details about the crime. Her research revealed that Harrison was disciplined for drunkenness and amnesia before being posted to a reserve combat unit in Northern Ireland. The execution of Harrison was botched, with the rope strangling him for 20 minutes instead of causing a swift death.  **Kalotschke's** findings have brought new understanding and closure to the case and its impact on the Wylie family.

recent_articles.title: Rupali Chakankar appears before SIT in 'godman' Kharat case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rupali Chakankar**, NCP leader and former State women’s panel chief, appeared before the special investigation team (SIT) in Nashik to answer questions about her alleged association with self-styled godman **Ashok Kharat**.  Ms. Chakankar resigned from both positions following revelations of her ties to **Kharat**, who is currently under arrest for rape and sexual exploitation. The Maharashtra Government has set up an SIT to investigate 12 cases against **Kharat** in Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts, with the SIT likely to question Ms. Chakankar about her connection to him.  Senior Congress leader **Nana Patole** alleged that **Kharat**’s life is in danger in prison and demanded the removal of four ministers connected to him from the state cabinet.

recent_articles.title: This is the sentence that protects every abuser in Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A pervasive societal stigma, "Sharif aurat thaney nahi jaati," prevents women from seeking justice at police stations in Pakistan. This belief system, often fueled by family pressure and a fear of social repercussions, discourages women from reporting domestic violence, harassment, or other crimes. Despite the existence of legal frameworks like the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act and provisions within the Pakistan Penal Code, many women choose to avoid seeking help at police stations due to this ingrained prejudice.  This societal barrier hinders the ability of law enforcement institutions to effectively address the widespread issue of violence against women.

recent_articles.title: Eluru pastor arrested under POCSO Act for sexual assault of minor - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chavatapalli Rambabu alias Hosanna**, a prayer house operator in Eluru district, has been arrested for allegedly raping and impregnating a minor girl. The girl's mother reported the incident to police, alleging that Rambabu gave her daughter a heavy dose of pills to terminate the pregnancy. **Eluru District Superintendent of Police K. Pratap Shiva Kishore** confirmed the arrest under the POCSO Act and other relevant sections.  The accused will be produced in court.

recent_articles.title: Pallegama Hemarathana Thero: Buddhist monk arrested for alleged rape of teen in Sri Lanka
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Venerable Pallegama Hemarathana Thero**, a high-ranking Buddhist monk and chief prelate of eight sacred sites in Sri Lanka, has been arrested for the alleged rape and sexual assault of a 15-year-old girl. The arrest followed criticism from the country's child protection authority regarding police inaction against him.  The monk is currently awaiting trial on May 12th. His mother was also arrested and remanded to custody for aiding and abetting the abuse.

recent_articles.title: Chirayu Rana's attorney says he did not fake father's death, it was about a 'dad-like figure' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chirayu Rana**, a former JPMorgan Chase employee, is embroiled in controversy after filing a lawsuit against **Lorna Hajdini**, alleging sexual harassment.  **Rana's** attorney, Daniel Kaiser, denies the allegations and claims attempts are being made to defame his client. **Rana** has worked for several financial institutions including **Carlyle Group**, **Morgan Stanley**, and **Apollo Global Management**, before joining JPMorgan Chase in 2024. The lawsuit alleges that **Hajdini** invited a witness to a threesome, which prompted **Rana's** withdrawal of the initial complaint but was later refiled.

recent_articles.title: Police to step up surveillance of abandoned properties as rape attempt case renews safety fears - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kochi City police** have launched a mission to identify and monitor vulnerable spots that could become criminal shelters following a recent rape attempt in an abandoned building.  The incident, which involved three men attacking a woman after her male friend was held at knifepoint, has raised concerns about the safety risks posed by abandoned buildings, overgrown premises, and poorly lit areas across the city. District Police Chief (Kochi City) Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar said police teams have been conducting inspections to assess security risks.
